subject: Re: Proposed staggered-notice approach & TFC carve-in for CloudPort order
messages:
From: Ruth Palmer <ruth.palmer@cloudport.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Josh Lin <josh.lin@cloudport.com>, CloudPort Legal <legal@cloudport.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CloudPort - order form and MSA: notice windows & TFC ask

Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Procurement and Legal at CloudPort asked us to put a couple of items on the table before we finalize the order form: primarily the auto-renew cadence and a termination-for-convenience (TFC) carve that covers the initial pilot SKUs.

High-level asks from CloudPort:
- Auto-renew: prefer 12-month renewals but need an option to opt-out with 45 days' written notice before renewal for the first two renewal cycles.
- TFC: want an explicit TFC during the pilot (first 6 months) with 60 days' notice and pro-rated credits for prepaid fees; they'd prefer this be tied to specific SKUs in the order form rather than the whole subscription.
- Notice windows: procurement requires a clear timeline matrix in the order form (renewal notice / invoice cutoff / service end) so they can align internal billing.

I've attached a redline of the MSA and the latest order form. Would Redwood consider a staggered approach (pilot SKUs with different termination mechanics than core services) to keep both teams comfortable?

We'd like to turn this around within 72 hours if possible — if Redwood needs a different approach, let us know what tradeoffs you require (fees, notice length, or data-handback).

Best,
Ruth
Ruth Palmer
Head of Procurement, CloudPort

Attachments: CloudPort_MSA_redlines_20260811.docx, OrderForm_CloudPort_v3_clean.pdf

From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudPort - order form and MSA: notice windows & TFC ask

Folks — forwarding CloudPort's asks. They want a staggered/sku-level TFC for pilot SKUs and a shortened opt-out window for the first two renewals. Attached redline from their side. Can you both weigh in on what we can offer without exposing revenue or setting a precedent?

What I think we need:
- A proposed compromise on the auto-renew notice (their 45 days vs our standard 90 days)
- A clear definition of which SKUs constitute the pilot and language tying TFC to those SKUs only (not the entire MSA)
- If we accept pro-rated credits, what's the calculation and cap?

I've got a customer call at 4pm PT tomorrow; it'd be ideal to have suggested language and a short rationale to share.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---- Original message attached ----

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudPort - order form and MSA: notice windows & TFC ask

Camila / Marissa — thanks for flagging. Quick read and proposed commercial/legal compromise below. My recommendation balances risk while giving CloudPort the flexibility they want during the pilot.

Proposed position (summary):
- Auto-renew: Annual renewals remain standard. For the first two renewal cycles, accept a 60-day opt-out notice (compromise between their 45d and our 90d). We should require opt-out in writing and include a single one-time administrative processing fee (nominal) if they exercise opt-out.
- TFC carve (pilot SKUs only): Accept an explicit TFC for identified pilot SKUs during the first 6 months post-commencement, with 60 days' notice. TFC limited to SKU charges (no refund of professional services, usage overage, or third-party marketplace fees).
- Credits: Pro-rate prepaid fees for the unused portion of the impacted SKUs on a straight-line basis, capped at the equivalent of 3 months' fees for those SKUs.
- Notice matrix: We'll add a short table to the order form that maps: renewal effective date / renewal notice cutoff / invoice cutoff / service end date.

Draft language snippet for MSA/order form (for legal redline):
"Termination for Convenience — Pilot SKUs. Notwithstanding Section X, Customer may terminate for convenience, with sixty (60) days' prior written notice, those product SKUs identified as 'Pilot SKUs' on the Order Form for a period of six (6) months following Service Commencement. Upon such termination Customer shall be entitled to a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable solely to the terminated Pilot SKUs, calculated on a straight-line basis and capped at an amount equal to three (3) months of fees for the terminated Pilot SKUs. This termination right shall not apply to professional services fees, usage-based charges incurred prior to termination, or third-party fees."
Operational asks: please confirm the administrative fee amount we want to propose (suggest $500 one-time) and validate the cap with finance. Also want Markus to check the snippet for legal risk and redline.

Karthik
Head of Legal Ops (acting), Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudPort - order form and MSA: notice windows & TFC ask

All — I like the compromise. Two quick asks:
1) Markus, can you confirm this language won't create a broader TFC exposure for other customers if we accept it? I want legal to lock language so it's SKU-scoped and does not create a carveout in the MSA more generally.
2) Camila — please tell CloudPort we'll propose 60-day opt-out for first two renewals and an administrative processing fee of $500. That gives us a reasonable revenue guardrail.

Timetable: we should get legal redline back within 24 hours if possible so Camila can update the customer during the 4pm call tomorrow.

-Marissa
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Josh Lin <josh.lin@cloudport.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudPort - order form and MSA: notice windows & TFC ask

Camila / team / Josh — attaching my quick redline notes and a one-paragraph rationale you can share with the customer. High-level: the proposed MSA snippet is acceptable if we strictly limit the TFC to SKUs listed on the order form and explicitly exclude data-processing, professional services, and usage charges. The cap and 60-day notice are reasonable commercial concessions.

Suggested short rationale to share with CloudPort:
"We can accommodate a pilot-specific termination right to help you validate the integration, while keeping the wider commercial terms intact. To minimize operational and revenue disruption we propose limiting the right to the SKUs listed on the Order Form, a 60-day written notice requirement, and a capped pro-rata refund of prepaid SKU fees. Professional services and usage charges are excluded. This approach keeps the MSA consistent for other customers while giving CloudPort the pilot flexibility they need."

Next steps (for Camila):
- Share legal snippet and rationale with CloudPort during the 4pm call.
- If CloudPort accepts, we'll produce a clean Order Form that enumerates Pilot SKUs and include the notice matrix.
- Finance will confirm the 3-month cap operationally; Marissa to coordinate.

Attachment: MSA_redline_markus_comments_20260812.docx

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
